summary: A robber who changes what he stole, like making wood into vessels, pays what it was worth when he stole it. All robbers pay by the value at the time of the robbery.

chunks.en: Someone who robs wood
chunks.st: In the case of one who robs another of wood

chunks.en: and makes it into vessels,
chunks.st: and fashions it into vessels,

chunks.en: or wool and makes it into clothes,
chunks.st: or one who robs another of wool and fashions it into garments,

chunks.en: pays what it was worth when he robbed it.
chunks.st: he pays the robbery victim according to the value of the goods at the time of the robbery, but he need not return the vessels or garments.
chunks.stMore: He has acquired the stolen items because they had undergone a change.

chunks.en: If he robbed a cow that was expecting a calf,
chunks.st: If one robbed another of a pregnant cow

chunks.en: and it gave birth, or a sheep full of wool,
chunks.st: and it then gave birth while in his possession, or if one robbed another of a ewe that was laden with wool

chunks.he: וּגְזָזָהּ, מְשַׁלֵּם דְּמֵי פָרָה הָעוֹמֶדֶת לֵילֵד,
chunks.en: and he sheared it, he pays the value of a cow about to give birth,
chunks.st: and the robber then sheared it, the robber pays the value of a cow that is ready to give birth

chunks.en: and the value of a sheep about to be sheared.
chunks.st: or the value of a ewe that is ready to be shorn.
chunks.stMore: He pays the value of the animal at the time of the robbery, and the calf or the wool remains his.

chunks.en: If he robbed a cow,
chunks.st: If one robbed another of a cow,

chunks.en: and it became pregnant by him and gave birth,
chunks.st: and it became pregnant in his possession, and it then gave birth;

chunks.en: or a sheep, and it grew wool by him and he sheared it,
chunks.st: or if one robbed another of a ewe, and it became laden with wool in his possession, and he then sheared it,

chunks.en: he pays what it was worth when he robbed it.
chunks.st: then the robber pays according to the value of the animal at the time of the robbery.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.en: All robbers pay what it was worth when they robbed it.
chunks.st: All robbers pay according to the value of the stolen item at the time of the robbery.

summary: If what was stolen got older or spoiled, the robber pays its value from when he stole it. But if it only lost value in a way you can't see, he may give it back as it is.

chunks.en: If he robbed an animal and it got old,
chunks.st: If one robbed another of an animal and it aged while in his possession, consequently diminishing its value,

chunks.en: or servants, and they got old,
chunks.st: or if one robbed another of Canaanite slaves and they aged while in his possession, they have been changed.

chunks.en: he pays what it was worth when he robbed it.
chunks.st: The robber therefore pays according to the value of the stolen item at the time of the robbery.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: with servants, he says to him,
chunks.st: With regard to Canaanite slaves, he says to the robbery victim:

chunks.en: "Here is yours in front of you."
chunks.st: That which is yours is before you.

chunks.en: If he robbed a coin and it cracked,
chunks.st: If one robbed another of a coin and it cracked, thereby reducing its value;

chunks.en: fruit and it rotted,
chunks.st: or if one robbed another of produce and it rotted;

chunks.en: wine and it turned sour,
chunks.st: or if one robbed another of wine and it fermented,

chunks.en: he pays what it was worth when he robbed it.
chunks.st: then he pays according to the value of the stolen item at the time of the robbery.

chunks.en: If a coin was made no good by the king,
chunks.st: If he robbed another of a coin and it was invalidated by the government;

chunks.en: terumah and it became tamei,
chunks.st: or if he robbed another of teruma and it became ritually impure;

chunks.en: chametz and Pesach passed over it,
chunks.st: or if he robbed another of leavened bread and Passover elapsed over it, and therefore it is prohibited to derive benefit from it;

chunks.en: an animal that was used for an aveirah,
chunks.st: or if he robbed another of an animal and a sin was performed with it, thereby disqualifying it for use as an offering;

chunks.en: or it became unfit for the mizbe'ach,
chunks.st: or if the animal was disqualified from being sacrificed upon the altar for some other reason;

chunks.en: or it was going out to be stoned:
chunks.st: or if the animal was going out to be stoned because it gored and killed a person at some point after the robbery,

chunks.en: he says to him,
chunks.st: the robber says to the robbery victim:

chunks.en: "Here is yours in front of you."
chunks.st: That which is yours is before you.
chunks.stMore: In all of these cases, although the value of the stolen item has been diminished or altogether lost, since the change is not externally discernible, the robber returns the item in its current state.

summary: Workers who ruin what they were given to fix must pay. A builder who breaks the stones of a wall he is knocking down must pay, unless it fell on the other side by itself.

chunks.en: If he gave things to craftsmen to fix,
chunks.st: If one gave items to craftsmen to fix

chunks.en: and they ruined them, they must pay.
chunks.st: and they damaged them, the craftsmen are liable to pay for the damage.

chunks.en: If he gave a carpenter a chest,
chunks.st: For example, if one gave a chest,

chunks.en: a box, or a cabinet to fix,
chunks.st: a box, or a cabinet to a carpenter to fix,

chunks.en: and he ruined it, he must pay.
chunks.st: and he damaged it, he is liable to pay.

chunks.he: וְהַבַּנַּאי שֶׁקִּבֵּל עָלָיו לִסְתֹּר אֶת הַכֹּתֶל,
chunks.en: And a builder who agreed to knock down the wall,
chunks.st: And a builder who committed to demolish a wall

chunks.en: and he broke the stones or did damage,
chunks.st: and while demolishing it he broke the stones, or who damaged them,

chunks.en: must pay.
chunks.st: is liable to pay.

chunks.en: If he was knocking down this side,
chunks.st: If he was demolishing on this side of the wall,

chunks.en: and it fell from the other side,
chunks.st: and the wall fell from another side and caused damage,

chunks.en: he does not pay. But if it was because of his hit, he must pay.
chunks.st: he is exempt from liability. But if a stone fell and caused damage due to the force of the blow, he is liable.

summary: If a dyer ruins wool, he pays for the wool. If he dyes it badly or the wrong color, the Rabbis discuss how much the owner pays him.

chunks.en: Someone who gives wool to a dyer,
chunks.st: In the case of one who gives wool to a dyer

chunks.en: and the pot burned it,
chunks.st: and it was burned in the cauldron during the dyeing process, thereby completely ruining the wool so that there is no enhancement, only loss,

chunks.en: he gives him the value of his wool.
chunks.st: the dyer gives the owner the value of his wool.

chunks.en: If he dyed it ugly,
chunks.st: If he dyed it unattractively [ka’ur] so that the dye is not absorbed well by the wool,

chunks.en: if the gain is more than the cost,
chunks.st: if the enhancement, i.e., the amount that the value of the wool has increased by being dyed, exceeds the dyer’s expenses,

chunks.en: he gives him the cost,
chunks.st: the owner of the wool gives the dyer the expenses.

chunks.en: and if the cost is more than the gain,
chunks.st: And if the expenses exceed the enhancement,

chunks.en: he gives him the gain.
chunks.st: he gives him the value of the enhancement.

chunks.en: If it was to dye it red,
chunks.st: If the owner gave wool to a dyer to dye it red for him

chunks.en: and he dyed it black,
chunks.st: and instead he dyed it black,

chunks.en: or black, and he dyed it red,
chunks.st: or to dye it black and he dyed it red,

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: he gives him the value of his wool.
chunks.st: The dyer gives the owner of the wool the value of his wool.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: if the gain is more than the cost,
chunks.st: Here too, if the value of the enhancement exceeds the dyer’s expenses,

chunks.en: he gives him the cost,
chunks.st: the owner of the wool gives the dyer the expenses.

chunks.en: and if the cost is more than the gain,
chunks.st: And if the expenses exceed the enhancement,

chunks.en: he gives him the gain.
chunks.st: he gives him the value of the enhancement.

summary: A robber who swore falsely that he did not steal, and wants to do teshuvah, must bring the money to the person he robbed, even very far away.

chunks.en: Someone who robs his friend of something worth a perutah,
chunks.st: One who robs another of an item having the value of at least one peruta

chunks.en: and swore to him that he didn't,
chunks.st: and takes a false oath to the robbery victim claiming his innocence,
chunks.stMore: and then later wishes to repent,

chunks.en: must bring it after him, even to Madai.
chunks.st: must bring the money, which includes the principal together with an additional one-fifth payment, to the robbery victim, even if this necessitates following after him to a distant place like Media.

chunks.he: לֹא יִתֵּן לֹא לִבְנוֹ וְלֹא לִשְׁלוּחוֹ,
chunks.en: He may not give it to his son or to his messenger,
chunks.st: The robber may not give the payment to the robbery victim’s son to return it to the robbery victim, and neither may he give it to his agent,

chunks.en: but he may give it to a messenger of beis din.
chunks.st: but he may give the payment to an agent of the court.

chunks.en: And if he died,
chunks.st: And if the robbery victim dies,

chunks.en: he gives it back to his heirs.
chunks.st: he returns it to his heirs.

summary: When a robber who swore falsely must still chase after the person he robbed: only if what is left is part of the stolen money itself, worth at least a perutah.

chunks.en: If he gave him the stolen money but did not
chunks.st: If he gave the robbery victim the principal value of the stolen item

chunks.en: give him the extra fifth,
chunks.explain: The robber who swore falsely adds an extra fifth.
chunks.st: but did not give him the additional one-fifth payment,

chunks.en: or he forgave him the stolen money but not
chunks.st: or if the owner forgave him concerning the principal

chunks.en: the fifth,
chunks.st: but did not forgive him concerning the additional one-fifth payment,

chunks.he: מָחַל לוֹ עַל זֶה וְעַל זֶה
chunks.en: or he forgave him for both,
chunks.st: or if he forgave him concerning this and concerning that,

chunks.en: except less than a perutah's worth of the stolen money,
chunks.st: with the exception of the value of less than one peruta of the principal,

chunks.en: he does not need to go after him.
chunks.st: he need not pursue him to repay the remaining debt.

chunks.en: If he gave him the fifth but did not
chunks.st: By contrast, if he gave the robbery victim the additional one-fifth payment

chunks.en: give him the stolen money,
chunks.st: but did not give him the principal,

chunks.en: or he forgave him the fifth but not
chunks.st: or if the robbery victim forgave him concerning the additional one-fifth payment

chunks.en: the stolen money,
chunks.st: but did not forgive him concerning the principal,

chunks.en: or he forgave him for this and
chunks.st: or if he forgave him concerning this and concerning

chunks.en: that, except a perutah's worth of the stolen money,
chunks.st: that, with the exception of the value of one peruta of the principal,

chunks.en: he must go after him.
chunks.st: he must pursue him to repay the remaining debt.

summary: Someone who swore falsely about money he owes, and then admits it, pays the money, an extra fifth, and brings a korban asham. If witnesses prove it instead, he pays only the money.

chunks.en: He gave him the stolen money,
chunks.st: If the robber gave the robbery victim the principal

chunks.en: and swore to him about the fifth,
chunks.st: and took a false oath to him concerning the additional one-fifth payment, asserting that he had already paid it, then the additional one-fifth is considered a new principal obligation.

chunks.he: הֲרֵי זֶה מְשַׁלֵּם חֹמֶשׁ עַל חֹמֶשׁ,
chunks.en: so he pays a fifth on top of the fifth,
chunks.st: The robber pays an additional one-fifth payment apart from the additional one-fifth payment about which he had taken a false oath.

chunks.he: עַד שֶׁיִּתְמַעֵט הַקֶּרֶן פָּחוֹת מִשָּׁוֶה פְרוּטָה.
chunks.en: until the main amount is less than a perutah.
chunks.st: If he then takes a false oath concerning the second one-fifth payment, he is assessed an additional one-fifth payment for that oath, until the principal, i.e., the additional one-fifth payment about which he has most recently taken the false oath, is reduced to less than the value of one peruta.

chunks.en: And the same with something left to be watched,
chunks.st: And such is the halakha with regard to a deposit,

words.note: Something one person gives another to keep safe.

chunks.en: as it says, "With a deposit, or with a loan
chunks.st: as it is stated: “If anyone sins, and commits a trespass against the Lord, and he defrauds his counterpart with regard to a deposit, or with regard to a pledge,

chunks.he: יָד אוֹ בְגָזֵל אוֹ עָשַׁק אֶת
chunks.en: or with robbery, or he cheated
chunks.st: or with regard to a robbery, or if he exploited his counterpart;

chunks.he: עֲמִיתוֹ אוֹ מָצָא אֲבֵדָה וְכִחֶשׁ בָּהּ
chunks.en: his friend, or he found a lost item and denied it,
chunks.st: or he has found that which was lost, and deals falsely with it,

chunks.en: and swore falsely":
chunks.st: and swears to a lie…he shall restore it in full, and shall add the fifth part more to it” (Leviticus 5:21–24).

chunks.he: הֲרֵי זֶה מְשַׁלֵּם קֶרֶן וָחֹמֶשׁ וְאָשָׁם.
chunks.en: this one pays the money, a fifth, and a korban asham.
chunks.explain: An asham is a korban brought for this kind of sin.
chunks.st: This one must pay the principal and an additional one-fifth payment, and bring a guilt-offering.

words.note: A korban brought to make up for certain sins.

chunks.en: "Where is my deposit?"
chunks.st: If the owner asked the bailee: Where is my deposit?

chunks.en: He said to him, "It got lost."
chunks.st: And the bailee said to him: It was lost.

chunks.en: "I make you swear,"
chunks.st: And the owner said: I administer an oath to you,

chunks.en: and he said, "Amen."
chunks.st: and the bailee said: Amen, therefore accepting the oath;

chunks.en: And the witnesses say that he ate it:
chunks.st: and the witnesses testify about the bailee that he consumed it,

chunks.en: he pays the money.
chunks.st: then he must pay the principal.

chunks.en: If he admitted by himself,
chunks.st: If the bailee admitted on his own that he had taken a false oath,

chunks.en: he pays the money, a fifth, and an asham.
chunks.st: then he must pay the principal and the additional one-fifth payment, and bring a guilt-offering.

summary: If the watchman said the deposit was stolen and swore, and witnesses prove he stole it himself, he pays double. If he admits by himself, he pays the money, a fifth, and an asham.

chunks.en: "Where is my deposit?"
chunks.st: If the owner asked the bailee: Where is my deposit, and the bailee

chunks.en: He said to him, "It was stolen."
chunks.st: said to him: It was stolen; and the owner said:

chunks.en: "I make you swear,"
chunks.st: I administer an oath to you,

chunks.en: and he said, "Amen."
chunks.st: and the bailee said: Amen, therefore accepting the oath;

chunks.en: And the witnesses say that he stole it:
chunks.st: and the witnesses testify about the bailee that he stole it,

chunks.en: he pays double.
chunks.st: he must pay the payment of double the principal.

chunks.en: If he admitted by himself,
chunks.st: If the bailee admitted on his own that he had taken a false oath,

chunks.en: he pays the money, a fifth, and an asham.
chunks.st: then he must pay the principal, the additional one-fifth payment, and bring a guilt-offering.

summary: A son who robbed his father and swore falsely, and then his father died, must give the money and a fifth to the other heirs and not keep his share.

chunks.en: Someone who robs his father,
chunks.st: The mishna continues: In the case of one who robs his father and the father demands that he return the stolen item,

chunks.en: and swore to him,
chunks.st: and he takes an oath to his father that he did not rob him;

chunks.en: and he died: this one pays the money
chunks.st: and then the father dies; and then the son admits that he robbed him and took a false oath, necessitating the return of the principal and the giving of the additional one-fifth payment to his father’s heirs, of which he is either one of several or the only one; what should he do?

chunks.en: and a fifth to his sons or to his brothers.
chunks.st: This son pays the principal and the additional one-fifth payment to his father’s sons or brothers, and brings a guilt-offering and does not keep his own share.

chunks.en: And if he does not want to,
chunks.st: And if he does not want to forfeit his share

chunks.en: or he does not have money,
chunks.st: or where he does not have sufficient funds to pay the other heirs while forfeiting his share,

chunks.en: he borrows, and the lenders come and get paid.
chunks.explain: They get paid from his share.
chunks.st: he borrows money in the amount of the value of the stolen item and the creditors come and are repaid in part from his share in the stolen item.

summary: If a father makes a vow that his son may not benefit from his things, the son still inherits him. But if he said "in my life and in my death," the son may not inherit.

chunks.en: Someone who says to his son,
chunks.st: In the case of one who says to his son in a vow: It is forbidden

chunks.en: "Konam, you may not benefit from what is mine":
chunks.explain: Konam is a word used to make a neder.
chunks.st: like an offering [konam], and for that reason you may not derive benefit from my property,

words.note: A word used to make a vow (neder).

chunks.en: if he dies,
chunks.st: if the father then dies

chunks.en: the son inherits him. "In my life and in my death":
chunks.st: the son inherits from him, because it is no longer the father’s property once he dies. The mishna continues: If the father stated in his vow that his son may not derive benefit from his property in his life and in his death,

chunks.en: if he dies,
chunks.st: then even if the father then dies

chunks.en: he does not inherit him,
chunks.st: the son does not inherit from him, as the prohibition is still in effect.

chunks.en: and he gives it back to his sons or to his brothers.
chunks.st: And instead of taking his inheritance, he returns his portion in the estate to his sons or to his brothers.

chunks.en: And if he has nothing,
chunks.st: And if he does not have sufficient funds to subsist without his inheritance,

chunks.en: he borrows, and the lenders come and get paid.
chunks.st: he borrows money in the amount of the value of his share in the inheritance and the creditors come and are repaid from his share.

summary: If someone robbed a ger and swore falsely, and the ger died with no family, the money goes to the Kohanim. The mishnah teaches what happens if the robber dies on the way.

chunks.en: Someone who robs a ger and swore to him,
chunks.st: With regard to one who robs a convert and takes a false oath denying having done so,

chunks.en: and the ger died: this one pays the money
chunks.st: and then the convert dies, the robber, in order to achieve repentance, pays the principal, i.e., the stolen item or, if it is no longer extant, its monetary value,

chunks.en: and a fifth to the Kohanim, and an asham on the mizbe'ach,
chunks.st: and an additional one-fifth of its value to the priests, and presents a guilt-offering to the altar,

chunks.en: as it says, "And if
chunks.st: as it is stated: “

chunks.en: the man has no relative to give back the payment to,
chunks.st: But if the man has no kinsman to whom restitution may be made for the guilt,

chunks.en: the payment given back to Hashem goes to the Kohen,
chunks.st: the restitution for guilt that is made shall be the Lord’s, even the priest’s;

chunks.en: besides the ram of atonement that
chunks.st: besides the ram of the atonement,

chunks.en: he will gain atonement with it."
chunks.st: whereby atonement shall be made for him” (Numbers 5:8).

chunks.he: הָיָה מַעֲלֶה אֶת הַכֶּסֶף וְאֶת הָאָשָׁם,
chunks.en: If he was bringing up the money and the asham,
chunks.st: If the robber was bringing the money and the guilt-offering up to Jerusalem

chunks.en: and he died, the money is given to his sons,
chunks.st: and he died before paying the priests and bringing his offering, the money shall be given to the robber’s children, and

chunks.en: and the asham grazes until it gets a mum,
chunks.explain: A mum is a blemish that makes it unfit for a korban.
chunks.st: the animal designated for the guilt-offering shall graze until it becomes blemished and consequently disqualified from being sacrificed.

chunks.en: and it is sold, and its money goes for nedavah.
chunks.explain: Nedavah: korbanos given as a gift.
chunks.st: And the animal shall then be sold and the money received for it shall be allocated for communal gift offerings.

summary: When the robber's money and his korban asham are given to the Kohanim, and in which order. He must give back what he stole before bringing the asham, but the extra fifth can come later.

chunks.en: If he gave the money to the Kohanim of the mishmar,
chunks.explain: A mishmar is the group of Kohanim serving that week.
chunks.st: If the robber gave the money to the members of the priestly watch

words.note: The group of Kohanim serving that week.

chunks.he: וּמֵת, אֵין הַיּוֹרְשִׁים יְכוֹלִין לְהוֹצִיא מִיָּדָם,
chunks.en: and he died, the heirs cannot take it back from them,
chunks.st: and then died before they sacrificed his guilt-offering, the heirs cannot remove the money from the priests’ possession,

chunks.en: as it says, "A man that
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And every man’s hallowed things shall be his;

chunks.en: gives to the Kohen, it is his."
chunks.st: whatsoever any man gives to the priest, it shall be his” (Numbers 5:10).

chunks.en: If he gave the money to Yehoyariv and the asham to Yedayah,
chunks.explain: Yehoyariv and Yedayah were groups of Kohanim.
chunks.st: The mishna continues: If the robber gave the money to the priestly watch of Joiarib and then gave the guilt-offering to the priestly watch of Jedaiah, the following priestly watch, to sacrifice on his behalf,

chunks.en: he did his duty. The asham to Yehoyariv and the money to Yedayah:
chunks.st: he has fulfilled his obligation. By contrast, if he first gave the guilt-offering to the priestly watch of Joiarib and then gave the money to the priestly watch of Jedaiah,

chunks.en: if the asham is still alive,
chunks.st: if the animal designated for the guilt-offering is extant,

chunks.en: the Kohanim of Yedayah should bring it as a korban,
chunks.st: then members of the priestly watch of Jedaiah, who received the money, should sacrifice it.

chunks.en: and if not,
chunks.st: But if it is no longer extant because the priestly watch of Joiarib had already sacrificed it,

chunks.en: he goes back and brings another asham,
chunks.st: he should return and bring another guilt-offering;

chunks.he: שֶׁהַמֵּבִיא גְזֵלוֹ עַד שֶׁלֹּא הֵבִיא אֲשָׁמוֹ,
chunks.en: because one who brings back what he robbed before bringing his asham
chunks.st: for one who brings his stolen item to the priests before he brings his guilt-offering

chunks.he: יָצָא. הֵבִיא אֲשָׁמוֹ עַד שֶׁלֹּא הֵבִיא גְזֵלוֹ,
chunks.en: did his duty. If he brought his asham before what he robbed,
chunks.st: has fulfilled his obligation, but one who brings his guilt-offering before he brings his stolen item

chunks.en: he did not do his duty.
chunks.st: has not fulfilled his obligation.

chunks.en: If he gave the main money but did not
chunks.st: Although he cannot sacrifice the offering before paying the principal, if he gave the principal

chunks.en: give the fifth,
chunks.st: but did not yet give the additional one-fifth payment,

chunks.en: the fifth does not hold him back.
chunks.st: the lack of having given the additional one-fifth payment does not preclude sacrificing the offering.
